- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) and forecast is trending up, shift forecast downward by 2–5% to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves when recent 3–5 day prices are trending down — model should lag slightly to avoid “over-leveraging” the signal.  
- If forecast consistently overshoots true outcome by >3% in early days of the 30d window, apply a 1–2% downward correction to the first 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating ±0.3–0.7), model should smooth out extreme swings — avoid forecasting 3–5 consecutive days with >10% deviation from mean.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model should not forecast further below 68 unless sentiment confirms strong bearish trend.  
- For sentiment history with high positive momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive >0.7), forecast should not exceed 10% above recent 5-day high — avoid “sentiment-driven overcorrection.”  
- If forecast is consistently 5–8% below true outcome over 30d, consider adding a 1–2% upward bias to the first 10 days to align with sentiment momentum.
